optionReasons.saa-med-267:option:0: PartiQL is only one SINTAXE SQL on the DynamoDB — without adequate index, or WHERE by Price continues to scan/filter.
optionReasons.saa-med-267:option:2: LSI can only be created JUNTO with the table — the table already exists; and the requirement says 'without creating new table''.
optionReasons.saa-med-267:option:3: FilterExpression filter DEPOIS to read — consumes the same scan capacity; and changing fate key requires re-create the table.

finalJustifications: Because one GSI with ProductCategory (partition) + Price (sort) transforms the search into Query Direct: exact match in the category and range (BETWEEN) in price — no scan and can be added to the existing table.
Because GSI index the price in a B tree within the table itself, accelerating the existing full scans without changing the way the application consults.
Because GSI makes the PartiQL optimize filters automatically, converting the scan into binary search on the indexed attributes of the inventory table.
Because GSI pre-calculates and materializes the results of the most frequent queries, serving the combinations category+direct price range of the index.

optionReasons.saa-med-273:option:0: Global Tables use ASSINCRONA replication — there is no 'atomic synchronous replication' between regions.
optionReasons.saa-med-273:option:1: Conditional writes per table + manual rollback in the application IS NOT atomic — the reversal may fail in the middle.
optionReasons.saa-med-273:option:3: Streams + Lambda is possible and unidirectional — without atomicity; replay reprocesses, does not reverse.

finalJustifications: Because TransactWriteItems executes even 100 operations in multiple items and TABELAS atomically (same region): or everything confirms, or everything is reversed — ACID Really?.
Because the transactions of DynamoDB block the entire tables during the operation, ensuring the isolation of the financial writings.
Because the TransactWriteItems replicates the writings in a synchronous way between regions, ensuring the global atomicity of the tables.
Because transactions dispense additional writing capacity — the cost is the same as simple non-transacional writings in the table.

optionReasons.saa-med-279:option:0: No standard alarm CloudWatch restarting RDS by CPU low.
optionReasons.saa-med-279:option:2: Automatic backups do not force reinstitution stopped — simply do not occur in the period.
optionReasons.saa-med-279:option:3: Court PARADA has no active standby taking over — Multi-AZ does not act on intentional stop.

finalJustifications: Because RDS limit stop to 7 DIAS: then automatically restarts to apply patches and pending maintenances — and the recovery returns to normal.
Because the AWS restarts the instance to verify if it is still necessary, charging the activity test of the stalled bank.
Because the limit of 7 days can be extended to 30 via support ticket, and the collection came from the unsolicited extension.
Because instances stopped by 7 days are converted into collectable snapshots, and reboot restores snapshot.

optionReasons.saa-med-281:option:0: The Auto Scaling of the provisions REAGE minutes late — sudden promotion peaks take throttling before adjustment.
optionReasons.saa-med-281:option:1: There is no 'Reserved + On-Demand covering peaks' in the same table — modes are excluded by table.
optionReasons.saa-med-281:option:3: Average capacity (5.000) waste 98% And take throttling at peaks — the worst of both worlds.

finalJustifications: Because with peak/valley ratio of 100:1 On-Demand wins: instantly adapts without throttling and collects by request — cheaper when the average use is much below the peak.
Because On-Demand has a unit price lower than that provided for in any volume — the AWS encourages management-free mode with reduced rate.
Because On-Demand reserves the 10.000 RCU/s from the peak permanently without extra cost, ready for any future promotion of the store.
Because On-Demand eliminates the limits by partitioning the table, letting the traffic of the peaks flow without sharding or internal capacity throttling.

optionReasons.saa-med-297:option:0: Scale-up postpones problem: OLTP row-based is not optimized for analytical scans — and BI would continue to compete with transactions.
optionReasons.saa-med-297:option:2: Cache Redis accelerates readings REPETIDAS — does not perform aggregations over billions of lines.
optionReasons.saa-med-297:option:3: The DynamoDB with GSIs is NoSQL by key — not analytical engine for BI.

finalJustifications: Because Redshift it's the data warehouse (column), MPP) designed for aggregations over billions of lines — the load OLAP Gets out of PostgreSQL and the transactional breathes.
Because Redshift automatically syncs with the RDS without any data load, mirroring the transactional tables.
Because Redshift executes the desires within itself RDS with hardware acceleration, without moving historical data.
Because Redshift is the serverless analytical version of PostgreSQL, running the aggregations in the same engine with identical syntax.

optionReasons.saa-med-045:option:1: Daily backup gives RPO up to 24 HORAS — 288x worse than the 5 minutes required; and restore everything bursts the RTO of 30 min.
optionReasons.saa-med-045:option:2: Multi-AZ protects within the region — regional disaster drops everything together.
optionReasons.saa-med-045:option:3: Active-active in total capacity ATENDE, but the budget explicitly does not involve duplicate production.

finalJustifications: Because the warm standby keeps the complete environment in reduced scale with continuous replication: failover in minutes (RTO 30 min ok) and minimum loss (RPO 5 min ok) per fraction of the cost of the asset.
Because the warm standby is completely off until the disaster, at no cost — the continuous replication happens directly in the storage of the AWS.
Because the warm standby serves users of both sites simultaneously, dividing the production load between the regions in normal operating times.
Because warm standby restores daily backups faster than normal strategy, thanks to preheated indices in the secondary region.

optionReasons.saa-med-049:option:0: rsync between instances is artisanal process — without isolated value or protection against account impairment.
optionReasons.saa-med-049:option:1: MIs in MESMA region and MESMA account falls along with compromised production.
optionReasons.saa-med-049:option:2: Snapshots in THEIR own production account are achievable by the intruder who compromised the account — exactly the risk to be eliminated.

finalJustifications: Because AWS Backup makes cross-region copy and native cross-account for an isolated vault (with optional Vault Lock) — the recommended pattern against ransomware and account commitment.
Because AWS Backup encrypts backups with a key that the production account doesn't know, nullifying ransomware access to copies.
Because AWS Backup detects ransomware patterns in the data and automatically locks the account before backups are reached by the attack.
Because AWS Backup records critical copies on physical tapes outside of AWS, the definitive isolation against commitment of account and region.

optionReasons.saa-med-293:option:0: The Snowball is a one-time physical data transfer — no continuous replication for DR.
optionReasons.saa-med-293:option:1: The Direct Connect is the LINK Network — does not replicate servers or recover them as EC2.
optionReasons.saa-med-293:option:3: The DMS migraine BANCOS OF DADOS — does not replicate entire servers at block level.

finalJustifications: Because the Elastic Disaster Recovery continuously replicates the servers in the block level to the AWS and recovers them as instances EC2 in minutes, with RPO of a few minutes.
Because DRS keeps instances EC2 identical connected in mirror 24/7, ready to take over traffic at the moment of disaster in the datacenter.
Because DRS converts physical servers to AMIs once a day, and recovery launches the latest images in the region.
Because DRS requires servers to already rotate VMware to replicate — the agent uses hypervisor snapshots as a block source.
